text:
Ashley (Acme): Hey team — we started seeing intermittent 502s from the hosted inference API during our nightly billing-sync at ~03:02 UTC. Bulk of requests succeed but ~6-8% fail with 502 gateway errors. Customer-side repro attached.

Sara (Support): acked — sorry you're hitting this, Ashley. Can you paste a minimal repro (curl) and tell us which SDK/version and auth method you're using? Also roughly how many concurrent requests in the job? :eyes:

Ashley (Acme): thanks. We're on the Node SDK v2.11.0, using API key auth. The job sends ~200 parallel requests in bursts (concurrency=200) over a 30s window. Minimal curl we used to reproduce locally: 

```bash
for i in {1..200}; do 
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"input":"test"}' \n    https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate &
 done; wait
```

When we run that against hosted endpoint we see a mix of 200 and 502. Full error body sometimes empty, sometimes: `\{"error":"gateway error"\}`

Miguel (Infra): thanks for the repro, Ashley. I pulled gateway logs around 2026-04-10 03:02 UTC for your account. I'm seeing a spike in upstream timeouts and a short burst of 502s from the edge LB -> runtime pool. Relevant log snippets: 

```
[2026-04-10T03:02:12Z] edge: request_id=abc123 account=acme route=/v1/generate svc=runtime pool=hosted-1 upstream_status=504 upstream_latency_ms=12000
[2026-04-10T03:02:13Z] edge: request_id=abc124 account=acme route=/v1/generate svc=runtime pool=hosted-1 upstream_status=502 upstream_latency_ms=0
[2026-04-10T03:02:14Z] runtime: instance=i-xyz task=generate queue_depth=198 kv_cache_miss=true
```

Miguel (Infra): hypothesis: burst of high concurrency caused request queueing on a subset of runtime workers; some requests were dropped by the edge LB when they couldn't establish a healthy upstream in time, producing 502s/504s. Also seeing your job is concentrated to a single region and hit a single autoscaling pool — you may be hitting a transient capacity wall.

Kevin (Engineering): adding some notes: our edge times out if the upstream connection establishment fails quickly (we return 502 in some races; 504 if upstream accepted then timed out). Two actionable items: (1) can you try smoothing the concurrency (stagger starts or reduce parallelism from 200 -> 50) and (2) enable SDK exponential backoff with jitter so a retry storm doesn't amplify the pressure.

Sara (Support): Ashley — can you try a quick experiment? 1) run the same curl loop but with concurrency=50, 2) then with 200 but add a small jitter sleep between launches: `sleep $(awk -v min=0.01 -v max=0.05 'BEGIN{srand(); print min+rand()*(max-min)}')` and share results. Also tell us if you have any long-lived connections (streaming) during the job.

Ashley (Acme): running tests now. With concurrency=50 we get 0 502s for 5 runs. With concurrency=200 + jitter we still see ~1-2% 502s (much lower than before). We do not use streaming for billing calls — completely stateless generates.

Miguel (Infra): good repro correlation. I'm going to check autoscaler logs for pool hosted-1 at that window — maybe scale-up lag. Also checking if there were any rolling restarts on the runtime sigs.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-20260410-195, severity=low-medium, owner=Miguel, summary="Intermittent 502s during customer billing-sync (concurrency spike)"

Miguel (Infra): quick update — autoscaler did trigger but we saw scale-up latency ~18-22s due to image pull throttling on a subset of hosts in that rack (rare). That means the initial burst landed on fewer warm instances. We're opening a follow-up with infra to prefer warm pool sizing for high-concurrency customer jobs.

Kevin (Engineering): engineering follow-up: runtime team will add a defensive admission policy so the edge can queue more gracefully and avoid immediate 502s for short scale events; also we can tune connection-establishment timeout heuristics for bursty workloads. This will take a few sprints but we can ship hotfixes for timeout thresholds this week if needed.

Sara (Support): Communication plan for Ashley / Acme: 1) ask them to temporarily reduce concurrency in nightly job (or add jitter) — low lift; 2) recommend Node SDK patch to v2.12.0 which turns on safe backoffs by default (we'll send upgrade link); 3) we’ll monitor their account for the next 48 hours and reach back with infra mitigation ETA.

Ashley (Acme): understood. We'll throttle to 50 for tonight and run a few gradual ramp tests. Could you also confirm there was no billing/charge impact or duplicate runs created because of retries? We didn't observe duplicates but worried SDK retries might have retried idempotent vs non-idempotent calls.

Kevin (Engineering): good call — our gateway attaches an idempotency token header if present; otherwise retries may cause duplicate generates. For billing-sync flows we recommend adding `Idempotency-Key` per entity. We'll include a note in the support explainer and the SDK upgrade.

Miguel (Infra): infra note — no billing/accounting anomalies from our side; only transient 502/504s. No extra tokens consumed beyond normal retries. I'll keep monitoring queue_depth and scale events for your account and post graphs.

Sara (Support): action items captured: 
- Ashley: throttle to 50 or add jitter tonight and run ramp tests (in progress)
- Ashley: upgrade SDK to v2.12.0 (safe backoff)
- Miguel: monitor autoscaler + post graphs (ETA 2h)
- Kevin: evaluate hotfix for edge timeout heuristics (ETA 48-72h)

Ashley (Acme): thank you — will run tests and report. Appreciate the quick triage. :heart:

Miguel (Infra): monitoring update (2h later): after Ashley throttled runs overnight, error rate dropped to <0.5%. Autoscaler warm-pool adjustments reduced scale-up latency to <6s for the observed windows. Leaving incident open to track engineering hotfix.

Sara (Support): leaving this thread open while Kevin evaluates the edge timeout fix. We'll update here when hotfix is deployed. For now mitigations: SDK upgrade + throttle/jitter + idempotency keys.

Kevin (Engineering): hotfix deployed to edge timeout config in canary region — monitoring for regressions. If stable, will roll to prod in next 6 hours.

Sara (Support): closing notes for Ashley: temporary mitigation validated, engineering hotfix in rollout, no billing duplication observed. Reopen thread if you see anomalies.

Ashley (Acme): all good on our side, no duplicates and nightly job stable after throttling. Thanks everyone! :tada:
